subject.title: [voice-call] OpenAI realtime: audio clipping / breaking inside words during first ~30s of outbound calls (Twilio mulaw output)

question: Should maintainers require current live Twilio/OpenAI audio evidence before changing the realtime Voice Call output pipeline, or sponsor a specific codec, gain, or pacing change now?
rationale: Source inspection confirms the supported path and plausible fix boundaries, but the audible failure mode cannot be localized without live audio or diagnostics, and changing this path affects all realtime telephony output.

options.title: Require live audio proof first
options.body: Keep this issue open until a maintainer or reporter captures a current redacted call artifact with peak/queue diagnostics, then fix the proven boundary.

options.title: Sponsor a narrow pipeline change now
options.body: Pick one owner boundary such as output headroom, u-law format, or pacer behavior and accept the regression risk of changing realtime call audio without current artifact proof.

options.title: Deprioritize as experimental voice-call work
options.body: Leave the issue open but treat it as lower priority until Voice Call realtime audio gets a broader stabilization pass.

recommendation.title: Require live audio proof first
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open until a maintainer or reporter captures a current redacted call artifact with peak/queue diagnostics, then fix the proven boundary.

likelyOwner.reason: Current blame and recent commits put the OpenAI realtime and Voice Call realtime bridge path under this contributor's recent work.
